Subject: Planned rolling kernel & NVIDIA driver upgrades — East US region (Mar 22)

Hi team and Acme ops,

We are scheduling a rolling maintenance for the East US region to deploy a kernel patch and updated NVIDIA driver bundle (v525.85 -> v535.12) to address a transient GPU memory leak observed under peak KV-cache workloads. High-level plan:

- Window: 2026-03-22 00:30 — 04:00 UTC (4-hour window).
- Scope: All hosted inference nodes in East US region; Dedicated pools with pinned hardware will be upgraded in a staggered fashion (control-plane coordinated).
- Impact: Each node will undergo a short restart; expected per-host disruption is 2–8 minutes while services drain and reconnect. We expect a small number of requests to see transient 503s if they hit a node during restart.
- Mitigations we will enable: graceful drain, retry-friendly headers, and temporary traffic steering to adjacent healthy nodes. Prefix caching and in-flight KV caches will be warmed back within 1–3 minutes after restart.

Customer ask: please confirm if your production traffic has a hard dependency on persistent websocket sessions that cannot tolerate 2–8 minute disconnects. If so, we can schedule a dedicated maintenance for your Dedicated pool outside the above window.

Attachments: maintenance_schedule.xlsx (per-pool timing), release_notes_v2.4.pdf (driver/kernel notes).

Next steps (internal):
- Marissa: publish status page & email notice to customers by EOD today.
- Rohan: include updated talking points for CS/SEs; prepare credits escalation criteria.
- Laura: confirm on-call rotation and escalation path.
- Hiro/Dylan: final canary plan and rollback criteria in INFRA-4532.

If Acme ops is OK with the window, we will proceed and send a final confirmation 48 hours before the start.

Thanks,
Hiro

Thanks all — final confirmations and brief technical notes below.

- Dedicated pools: we will stagger restarts. For single-tenant pools with <=10 hosts (eg dedicated-east-02) we will take one host offline at a time. For larger pools we will do 10% of hosts, then wait 10 minutes for metrics stabilization.
- Canary: three non-prod canaries will run 24 hours prior to the window (Mar 21, 00:30–01:30 UTC) and a small traffic canary in the window itself (first 30 minutes). If the canary fails, we abort and roll back to previous driver within 30 minutes.
- Rollback: driver rollback path validated; estimated time to full rollback across region 45–90 minutes depending on pool size.
- Escalation contact during maintenance: On-call infra pager: +1-415-555-0198 (primary), +1-415-555-0110 (secondary) and support channel redwood.com/support (live chat).

INFRA ticket: INFRA-4532 (runbook and per-pool timing attached). I attached the per-pool maintenance_schedule.xlsx and the release notes PDF for reference.

I'll post the runbook link to the ticket and update the status page draft. Laura/Marissa if you want a short blurb for customers I can propose one-liner text.
